thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: High error rate + CUDA OOMs on inference-serving cluster in us-west-2. Automated detection flagged 2000 errors/min and host flaps. Paging oncall.
alex: seeing same. spikes started ~4082468000. 502s, grpc errors, a handful of container restarts.
marta: putting last 5m graphs in threads (latency, 5xx). high p99 token latency too. any obvious infra changes?
jin: nothing in changelog. infra deploy at 4082466000 was small infra tag, not related. I see IB retransmit counters climbing on rack-7: `ibstat -s` shows retransmits++.
alex: kubectl logs from pod runtime-serve-9f8: ```
E tensorflow: cudnn status: CUDNN_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.2GiB (GPU 0; 16GiB total, 14.3GiB already allocated)
Stack: ...
``` 
alex: multiple pods show similar OOM traces, but they correlate with inter-node retransmits (packet dupes) — KV cache RPCs are timing out and retries blow memory usage.
marta: can we confirm network? `ibv_devinfo`/ifstat shows TX errors and late-acks on mlx5_0 on hosts node-72-*. jin, can you paste the ifstat and `ethtool -S`?
jin: short snippet: ```
# ifstat -i mlx5_0 1 1
       mlx5_0
 KB/s in  KB/s out
    120.4    111.9
# /sys/class/net/mlx5_0/statistics/tx_drops -> 0
# /sys/class/net/mlx5_0/statistics/tx_errors -> 482
# rdma counters: retransmits = 13k in 10m, late_acks = 9k
``` 
tilly: that matches the serving node flaps. when RDMA retransmits spike, RPCs for KV cache stall, runtime keeps allocating while waiting -> OOM cascade.
ops-bot: Auto-remediation attempted: node-72-3 NIC reset, container restart, autoscaler drained a node. Errors briefly dropped then climbed again.
alex: mitigation idea: 1) disable cross-node kvcache for affected models (force local-only), 2) reduce batching to single-request to avoid accumulation, 3) route traffic away from rack-7 to healthy racks.
marta: on that, I can flip model routing small canary: `routing.lockdown=true model=quant-small region=us-west-2 rack_avoid=rack-7` — doing it now.
jin: started cordon/drain on node-72-3 and node-72-4. `kubectl drain` kicking pods to other nodes. but if fabric is shared across rack, moving pods may not help much.
customer-success: any ETA on customer impact? we have alerts from a few enterprise customers reporting 5xxs.
alex: initial blamemap: affected models: embed-xlarge, chat-medium. ~12% of traffic in us-west-2 saw degraded responses in last 15m. Some customers reported latency > 120s or errors.
marta: posting status update to status.redwood.ai: "Investigating service degradation in us-west-2 affecting chat/embedding. Mitigations in progress."
incident-bot: STATUS: page routed to oncall. severity: SEV2 -> could be SEV1 if customer impact widens. current impact: partial customer failures, elevated latency, retries causing OOMs.
jin: doing NIC-level resets across rack-7 hosts and checking switch counters with netops. seeing flaps on ib-switch-7 port 12 (errdisable due to ecn?).
tilly: can we confirm whether ECN marking is causing retransmit storms? early suspicion: switch queue management misconfig after QoS change last week.
ops-bot: detected QoS rule change on switch-7 at 4082467200 (admin:netops). Reverting now.
alex: reverted rule looks promising — retransmits dropping by ~40% in last 60s. but we still see a few stuck pods with inflated memory.
marta: action list so far:
- netops revert QoS on switch-7 (done)
- cordon & drain node-72-3/4 (in progress)
- disable cross-node kvcache for embed-xlarge (in progress)
- reduce batching to single-request for chat-medium (scheduled)
- route traffic away from rack-7 (canary done)
- restart stuck pods after drain (pending)

jin: running `kubectl top pods` and killing pods with >90% GPU mem utilization to force restart. sample: `kubectl exec -it runtime-serve-9f8 -- kill -9 1` (will restart container)
alex: careful with kill, prefer graceful: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-serve --field-selector metadata.name=runtime-serve-9f8` — but if stuck, hard kill necessary.
customer-success: we got two enterprise tickets claiming model outputs aborted mid-generation, customers on dedicated capacity are OK. public API users hit failures.
tilly: that fits: dedicated pools were on other racks. priority: restore hosted inference ASAP and keep dedicated SLA.
oncall-next: I'll take next shift at handoff. need a short summary.
alex: handoff summary for oncall-next:
- root cause: spike in IB retransmits/late-acks on rack-7 after switch QoS change
- symptom: KV cache RPC stalls -> runtime waits & accumulates memory -> CUDA OOMs and container crashes
- impact: ~12% hosted traffic in us-west-2 degraded; some enterprise customers reported 5xxs; dedicated customers unaffected
- mitigation done: reverted QoS, cordoned 2 nodes, routing canary away from rack-7, reduced batch sizes for hot models, restarting high-mem pods
- next steps: netops to verify switch stability for 30m, monitor retransmit counters, consider permanent QoS rollback and reroute of critical racks, postmortem to include timeline and switch config diff

marta: adding runbook checklist items to the incident doc: IF RDMA retransmit spike -> revert recent switch changes, isolate rack, disable cross-node kvcache, reduce batching, drain nodes.
jin: netops confirms switch port flapped due to misapplied QoS policy; they will keep port in monitor for 2h.
ops-bot: Autoscaler note: we temporarily suspended scale-ups for runtime-serve to avoid triggering more cross-node allocations while fabric unstable.
incident-bot: PAGER: next escalation if errors > 1000/min for 10m.
customer-success: posting proactive message to affected customers: "We're investigating increased errors. Mitigations in place; we'll provide updates every 30m." done.
alex: current numbers: errors/min down from 2000 -> 320 in last 8m. retransmits down 70% after revert. memory pressure slowly falling as pods restart.
tonight: please join postmortem doc at /incidents/4082468100-pm-draft when we stabilize.
oncall-next: taking it. I'll be watching until 4092468100 and will escalate if counters tick up. TL;DR: netops change -> retransmit storm -> OOM cascade -> partial service degradation. handoff complete. :thumbsup:
